title: Ballistic Flight: Maximum Height
learningObjectives: Calculate maximum height as V0 squared divided by twice gravitational acceleration
Explain that horizontal motion has constant velocity and distance equals velocity times time

sources.title: Ballistic Flight Equations — NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics

evidence.quote: The horizontal motion is uniform because there is no external force in the horizontal direction.

explanations.text: With no horizontal force, horizontal velocity stays constant and horizontal distance grows linearly with time.

evidence.quote: In the vertical plane, weight is the only external force acting on the object.

explanations.text: Weight alone acts vertically, so vertical velocity decreases linearly with time according to gravitational acceleration.

evidence.quote: The maximum altitude changes as the square of the launch velocity.

explanations.text: Maximum height is reached when vertical velocity is zero and scales as the square of initial vertical velocity divided by twice gravity.
